name: Z → μ⁺μ⁻
explanation: A Z boson decays into a muon and its antimuon. The Z couples to a fermion and its own antiparticle, so the two decay products always have opposite charge.

name: Z → b b̄
explanation: A Z boson decays into a bottom quark and antiquark, a decay the Z shares with every other fermion type. Measuring the Z width at LEP showed there are exactly three light neutrino species.

name: β⁻ decay (quark level)
explanation: A down quark turns into an up quark by emitting a virtual W⁻, which becomes an electron and an electron antineutrino. Charge and electron lepton number are conserved at each vertex.

name: β⁺ decay (quark level)
explanation: An up quark turns into a down quark by emitting a virtual W⁺, which becomes a positron and an electron neutrino. It happens in proton-rich nuclei, where converting a proton to a neutron lowers the energy.

name: Muon decay μ⁻ → e⁻ ν̄ₑ ν_μ
explanation: A muon turns into a muon neutrino by emitting a virtual W⁻, which becomes an electron and an electron antineutrino. Muon and electron lepton numbers are each conserved, which is why a neutrino and an antineutrino of different families appear.

name: t → b W⁺
explanation: The top quark decays almost always into a bottom quark and a real W⁺ boson, because the other CKM couplings are tiny. It decays so fast that it never forms hadrons.

name: W⁻ → μ⁻ ν̄_μ
explanation: A W⁻ boson decays into a muon and a muon antineutrino. The W couples charged leptons only to their own neutrino family, so the neutrino must be the muon type.

name: e⁻ ν̄ₑ → W⁻ → μ⁻ ν̄_μ
explanation: An electron and an electron antineutrino fuse into a virtual W⁻, which decays into a muon and a muon antineutrino. Each lepton family number is conserved separately through the W.

name: τ⁻ → ν_τ d ū (hadronic decay)
explanation: A tau turns into a tau neutrino by emitting a virtual W⁻, which becomes a down quark and an up antiquark. The quarks bind into hadrons such as a π⁻.

name: Electron capture e⁻ u → ν_e d
explanation: An atomic electron is absorbed by an up quark in the nucleus, which turns into a down quark while a neutrino escapes. A proton becomes a neutron without emitting a positron.

name: ν_μ e⁻ → μ⁻ ν_e (charged current)
explanation: A muon neutrino hits an electron and exchanges a W⁺, turning into a muon while the electron turns into an electron neutrino. The lepton families swap partners but each family number is conserved.

name: ν_μ e⁻ → ν_μ e⁻ (neutral current)
explanation: A muon neutrino scatters elastically off an electron by exchanging a Z boson. Its discovery in 1973 confirmed the weak neutral current predicted by electroweak theory.

name: e⁺e⁻ → Z → ν ν̄
explanation: An electron and positron annihilate into a Z boson that decays into a neutrino pair. Photons do not couple to neutrinos, so only the Z can mediate this process.

name: π⁺ → μ⁺ ν_μ
explanation: The up quark and down antiquark in a π⁺ annihilate into a virtual W⁺, which decays into a muon and a muon neutrino. The decay to a muon is favored over an electron by helicity suppression.

name: K⁺ → μ⁺ ν_μ
explanation: The up quark and strange antiquark in a K⁺ annihilate into a virtual W⁺ that decays to a muon and a neutrino. The u–s coupling is suppressed by the CKM matrix element V_us, which is about 0.22.

name: Λ → p π⁻ (s → u d ū)
explanation: A strange quark in a Λ baryon turns into an up quark by emitting a virtual W⁻, which becomes a down quark and an up antiquark. The weak force changes strangeness by one unit, which is why Λ lives far longer than strong decays would allow.

name: D⁰ → K⁻ π⁺ (c → s u d̄)
explanation: A charm quark turns into a strange quark by emitting a virtual W⁺, which becomes an up quark and a down antiquark. The c → s transition is Cabibbo-favored, so this is a dominant D⁰ decay.

name: e⁺e⁻ → W⁺W⁻ (neutrino exchange)
explanation: An electron and positron produce a W pair by exchanging a virtual electron neutrino. Without the extra Z and photon diagrams, this cross-section would grow with energy and violate unitarity.

name: γγ → W⁺W⁻ (W exchange)
explanation: Two photons produce a W pair by exchanging a virtual W, because W bosons carry electric charge and couple to photons. A neutral photon pair becomes two charged particles of opposite sign.

name: γγ → W⁺W⁻ (contact vertex)
explanation: Two photons produce a W pair at a single four-point vertex. Gauge boson contact interactions like this one are required by the structure of the electroweak theory.
